prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean a site that (a) teaches crypto in plain English and (b) also publishes its own real trading/account numbers (including losses), or do you just want plain-English education plus a way to verify numbers yourself?

Short answer: there isn’t a single mainstream “best” site that cleanly combines beginner-friendly, plain-English teaching with fully public, auditable P&L that explicitly highlights losses. Most high-quality educators/news sites explain concepts well but don’t run a public trading account. If transparency about real gains and losses is critical, you’ll usually need to pair an education source with on‑chain/portfolio tools or follow individual creators who publish verifiable wallet addresses.

If you want immediate places to start
- Plain-English education (good for beginners)
  - Coin Bureau — long, clear explainer articles and videos geared to new users.
  - Bankless (newsletter + podcasts) — practical, step-by-step DeFi and crypto guides in accessible language.
  - Andreas M. Antonopoulos (books, videos) — excellent plain English explanations of fundamentals.
- Data and verifiable numbers
  - Etherscan / Solscan / blockchain explorers — view real on‑chain transactions and balances for any public address.
  - Zerion, DeBank, Zapper — portfolio viewers that show real positions (useful for verifying wallets).
  - Dune Analytics — community dashboards that publish verifiable on‑chain dashboards (can show trades, P&L for labeled wallets).
  - Glassnode / Messari — on‑chain metrics and charts (more advanced, but factual numbers).
- For “published losses” / transparency
  - Look for educators or traders who publish a verifiable public wallet address (or a Dune dashboard) and a linked portfolio tracker. That’s the reliable way to see their real trades and losses. Few big education sites do this by default.

How to verify someone truly “publishes losses”
1. They publish a public wallet address (or fund wallet addresses).
2. You can look up that address in a blockchain explorer or Zerion to see transaction history and current balances.
3. They publish a Dune dashboard or Google Sheet that aggregates P&L — dashboards with on‑chain data are best because the underlying transactions are auditable.
4. For funds, look for audited statements or public quarterly reports.

If you want, I can:
- Find a few beginner-friendly educators who also publish verifiable wallet addresses or Dune dashboards, or
- Recommend a one‑week learning path combining a plain-English course (Coin Bureau/Bankless) plus a Dune tutorial so you can verify trades yourself.

Which would you prefer?
